html:
The Koasati, or Coushatta, are a Muskogean-speaking people of the American Southeast. In the 1500s they lived on the Tennessee River, and later along the Alabama River, where they were one of the towns of the Creek confederacy. The town of Coste that Hernando de Soto passed in 1540 is often taken to be theirs.

After France gave up its North American colonies in 1763, many Koasati moved west into Spanish Louisiana and later Texas. Today there are three main groups:

  • the Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana, near Elton;
  • the Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas, who share a reservation with the closely related Alabama people;
  • Koasati within the Alabama-Quassarte Tribal Town in Oklahoma, among the Muscogee.

The Koasati language is still spoken in Louisiana.
